evidence: Films were grown by sequential exposures of bis(2,2,6,6-tetramethylheptane-3,5-dionate)nickel(II) [Ni(thd)2] and hydrogen sulﬁde (H2S) in the temperature range of 175–350 /C14 C. Due to lower vapor pressure of Ni(thd)2, it was dosed to reactor using ultrahigh purity N2 (99.999%) as carrier gas through the overhead assembly of the precursor bubbler. A continuous flow of 250 sccm of N2 was maintained using MKS mass flow controllers to retain a constant base pressure of /C24 1 Torr in the reactor during the reaction to maintain the laminar flow.
